analysis:
The PR is documentation-only. docs/provider/attestation.md changes the date (line 3) and adds one paragraph at head lines 142-143. docs/provider/cli-reference.md adds one bullet at head line 1025. The additions say that App Attest serving authorization can stay visible through its unexpired lease while MDM-removal readiness needs a fresh coordinator decision. They tell operators to keep existing profiles installed until a fresh decision arrives.

This matches the existing TB-011, T-053, T-054 and T-057 framing, where serving authorization and removal readiness are separate coordinator verdicts. The text is conservative. It does not grant authorization, weaken a gate or extend an Apple proof lifetime, and it does not claim a deployment. It does not change receipt policy, and it does not treat a local state file as trust evidence. It also restates that a state-file rewrite cannot extend readiness.

No code, wire protocol, key custody or routing changes appear. TB-002, TB-009 and the attestation and cache assumptions are unchanged.

Unverified contracts:
- The new text cites provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Diagnostics/ProviderAuthorizationReadiness.swift (`summary`) and docs/reference/provider-authorization.md. Neither file is in the supplied evidence, so I could not check that the behavior and link targets exist.
- A dangling or inaccurate reference is a documentation-accuracy risk, not a demonstrated security regression.
- The cli-reference.md change at base/head line 1022 is only a patch excerpt, but the hunk is complete.

No findings.
